record.what_it_does: Frontend cloud platform for deploying, hosting and managing web projects, domains and serverless infrastructure.
record.auth_notes: Methods: (1) Access tokens (Bearer, scoped to account, team or project) created by the user. (2) Vercel Integrations: the OAuth-style redirect `code` is exchanged at POST /v2/oauth/access_token. New integrations should use short-lived tokens (1h) via the client_credentials grant, because long-lived tokens are deprecated. (3) A "Sign in with Vercel" OAuth flow exists, but I did not fetch its docs. A multi-user toolkit would use an Integration install, with the teamId query param on requests, or user-pasted access tokens.
record.access_notes: Access tokens can be created on any account, including the free Hobby plan. I did not verify this on a pricing page. Creating an integration is self-serve through the Integrations Console form, and connectable-account integrations can be installed by external users straight away with a "Community" badge. Listing on the public marketplace needs 500+ installs and a review. Native Marketplace integrations need Vercel's approval. Some endpoints and features need Pro or Enterprise: account webhooks and the billing scope. Vercel MCP clients need CIMD or a review.
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST reference lists roughly 330 endpoints. They cover projects, deployments, domains/DNS/certs, env vars, teams, access groups, edge config, drains, webhooks, checks, integrations and billing. The count is an estimate from grepping the fetched page.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.vercel.com is a remote MCP server using OAuth and Streamable HTTP. It is available on all plans. Clients must use CIMD or be reviewed and approved by Vercel.
record.blocker_notes: There is a broad REST API with a self-serve integration or token path. Minor caveats: account webhooks and billing need Pro or Enterprise, and public marketplace listing needs review. No dedicated test mode was found, but a free Hobby account serves for testing.
